It uses only the\nRuby standard library plus SQLite, keeps domain logic in named modules under\n`lib/`, and implements a tiny TCP/HTTP layer under `lib/http/`.\n\n## Quick start\n\n```bash\nPORT=3000 ./run.sh\n```\n\n`run.sh` is a one-line wrapper that executes `ruby server.rb`. State, persistence, and routing\n\n### Persistence design\n\n- SQLite file: `game.db` in the working directory.\n- A single `Mutex` (`Persistence::DB_MUTEX`) serializes all database access.\n- Conventions for extending and testing\n\n### Adding a new endpoint\n\n1. If the endpoint is pure computation, put it in the appropriate domain\n   module (e.g., `PureRules`, `PlayerHandbook`, `DmTools`) and have it return\n   a Hash on success or `nil` on invalid input.\n2. If the endpoint needs persistence, add it to the module that owns the data\n   (e.g., `Combat`, `Campaigns`, `Compendium`, `PlayCampaigns`) and return a\n   `[:tag, data]` tuple.\n3. Wire the endpoint into `Router.route` with an explicit `method`/`path`\n   check and call `handle_result` or `json_response` / `error_response` as\n   needed.\n4. If the endpoint requires authentication, wrap the handler with\n   `with_auth(request, %w[role]) { |actor| ... }`.\n5. If the endpoint creates a resource, use status `201`; otherwise use `200`.\n\n### Adding a new table\n\n1. Add the `CREATE TABLE` statement to `Persistence::SCHEMA_SQL`.\n2. Add the table name to `Persistence::APP_TABLES` in dependency order.\n   `reset!` and `soft_reset!` derive their drop lists from this single source.\n3. 'dm' : 'player'\n\n      # The queue visualizes the full turn cycle: each player followed by a DM turn.\n      # The actual current actor is driven by `current_actor`, not by advancing this queue.\n      members = d.execute(\n        'SELECT username FROM play_campaign_members WHERE campaign_id = ? ORDER BY username',\n        campaign_id\n      ).map { |row| row[0] }\n\n      next [:conflict] if members.empty?\n\n      # The DM resolves a turn by advancing to the player who follows the one that\n      # submitted the most recent player-side turn (action or travel). Rest turns\n      # do not rotate the queue so a resting player keeps their place in the cycle.\n      last_action_row = d.get_first_row(\n        \"SELECT actor FROM play_narrations WHERE campaign_id = ? AND username = ?',\n      [campaign_id, username]\n    )\n    return false unless row\n\n    powers = JSON.parse(row[0])\n    row[1] == 1 && powers.include?(power)\n  rescue StandardError\n    false\n  end\n  private_class_method :active_delegate_with_power?\n\n  def self.turn(campaign_id, actor)\n    return [:invalid] unless campaign_id.is_a?(String) && !campaign_id.empty?\n\n    Persistence.db do |d|\n      campaign = d.get_first_row(\n        'SELECT owner, status, current_actor, turn_number FROM play_campaigns WHERE id = ?',\n        campaign_id\n      )\n      next [:not_found] unless campaign\n\n      owner, status, current_actor, turn_number = campaign\n      is_member = d.get_first_value(\n        'SELECT 1 FROM play_campaign_members WHERE campaign_id = ? 'dm' : 'player'\n\n      # The queue visualizes the full turn cycle: each player followed by a DM turn.\n      # The actual current actor is driven by `current_actor`, not by advancing this queue.\n      members = d.execute(\n        'SELECT username FROM play_campaign_members WHERE campaign_id = ?
